name: Scott Fitzgerald
bio: Scott Fitzgerald has represented Wisconsin's 5th Congressional District since 2021. He served in the Wisconsin State Senate from 1995 to 2021, including as majority leader, and earlier published a local newspaper. He spent 27 years in the U.S. Army Reserve, retiring as a lieutenant colonel, and grew up in Hustisford, Wisconsin.

platform.point: Lists fighting inflation and lowering costs as a leading priority of his office.
Backs policies for U.S. energy independence and opposed cancelling the Keystone XL pipeline.
Supports school choice through the School Choice Caucus and a bill requiring schools to post curricula publicly.
Lists election integrity as one of his issue priorities in Congress.
Highlights agriculture and veterans' services among his main issue areas.

economy.evidence: Opposes higher taxes on wealthy individuals and supports tax options for pass-through businesses.

welfare.evidence: OnTheIssues records support for work requirements for Medicaid recipients.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: supports a ban after 20 weeks and voted against the Women's Health Protection Act; guns: backed ending the 48-hour waiting period and opposes private-sale background checks.

security.evidence: OnTheIssues records support for tougher sentencing, including for juvenile offenders.

immigration.evidence: Opposes a path to citizenship for undocumented immigrants and supports immigration bans from non-cooperating countries.

foreign.evidence: Voted to support Israel after the October 7 attacks and backed applying the 2002 Iraq authorization to ISIS.

energy.evidence: Official site backs energy independence and opposed the cancellation of the Keystone XL pipeline.

education.evidence: Joined the School Choice Caucus and introduced a bill requiring public posting of school curricula.

faith.evidence: OnTheIssues records support for keeping religious references in public spaces.

notes: Energy, education and faith scores are newly added from his official site and OnTheIssues; many OnTheIssues entries date from his state Senate career.

name: Andrew Beck
current_role: Health-care product development leader and union member
bio: Andy Beck is the Democratic nominee for Wisconsin's 5th Congressional District and lives in West Bend. Born and raised in Milwaukee, he has worked in hospitality, as an MRI technologist and in product development at GE Healthcare, and holds an MBA from Cardinal Stritch University. He has not previously held elected office.

platform.point: Pledges to protect Social Security, Medicare and Medicaid.
Would seek federal protections for reproductive health care against political interference.
Proposes free trade-school training, called Quick Start Careers, to rebuild the middle class.
Offers an 'Afford to Grow' plan to widen access to affordable homeownership.
Lists action on climate change as a priority to protect communities.
Supports comprehensive reform pairing border security with humanitarian values.

economy.evidence: Campaign centres on union support, labor rights and government backing for farmers.

welfare.evidence: Pledges to protect Social Security, Medicare and Medicaid and expand mental health programs.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: supports congressional protections for reproductive rights.

immigration.evidence: Calls for comprehensive reform balancing border security with humanitarian values.

energy.evidence: Lists addressing climate change as a campaign priority.

education.evidence: Proposes publicly funded free trade-school education.

notes: Campaigns as Andy Beck; ballot name listed as Andrew Beck.

name: Glenn Grothman
bio: Glenn Grothman has represented Wisconsin's 6th Congressional District since 2015. He previously served in the Wisconsin State Assembly from 1993 to 2005 and the Wisconsin State Senate from 2005 to 2015. A graduate of UW-Madison and its law school, he practiced law in West Bend before entering politics.

platform.point: Says federal government should step back through deregulation and a simpler tax code to spur job growth.
Calls the southern border a crisis needing congressional action and belongs to the Border Security Caucus.
Holds that education decisions belong mainly to state and local governments, not Washington.
Backs career and technical training to fill skilled labor shortages.

economy.evidence: Seeks lower income and property taxes, opposes the estate tax and favors deregulation.

welfare.evidence: Has voted repeatedly to repeal the Affordable Care Act and proposed work requirements for welfare.

liberty.evidence: Same-sex marriage: backed a constitutional amendment banning it; abortion: opposes access; guns: co-wrote Wisconsin's concealed carry law.

security.evidence: OnTheIssues records opposition to government tracking via GPS, cellphones or social media.

immigration.evidence: Supports deporting undocumented immigrants, opposes sanctuary policies and opposed admitting Syrian refugees.

foreign.evidence: Voted against the 2024 Ukraine military aid package but for supporting Israel after October 7.

energy.evidence: Opposes federal wind and solar subsidies and renewable mandates and favors oil and gas drilling.

education.evidence: Supports school vouchers and opposed Common Core standards.

faith.evidence: Sponsored 'In God We Trust' license plates and supports a Judeo-Christian moral framework in public life.

notes: Several OnTheIssues entries date from his time in the state legislature.

name: Brad Smith
bio: Brad Smith is the Democratic nominee for Wisconsin's 6th Congressional District. He describes himself as a military veteran and business builder who attended college on the GI Bill, the first man in several generations of his family to earn a degree. He has not previously held elected office.

platform.point: Supports livable wages, stronger worker protections and tax rules favoring firms that keep jobs in Wisconsin.
Would protect the ACA, lower drug costs, expand rural care and build toward universal coverage via a public option.
Opposes automated license plate readers unless warrants, access limits and audits are in place.
Wants a lawful, humane system with more legal pathways and status options for long-settled workers.
Supports renewable energy, electrification and electric vehicles alongside conservation of public lands.
Calls for regulatory review, transparency rules and public input before data centers are built.

economy.evidence: Supports livable wages, stronger worker protections and tax rules tied to domestic job creation.

welfare.evidence: Supports building toward universal coverage through a public option.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: decisions belong to women and families; LGBTQ: supports marriage equality and anti-discrimination laws; guns: backs Second Amendment with safety measures.

security.evidence: Opposes license plate readers without warrant requirements, access limits and audits.

immigration.evidence: Supports expanded legal pathways and status options for established workers.

energy.evidence: Supports a transition to renewables, electrification and electric vehicles.

tech.evidence: Wants regulatory hurdles, transparency requirements and public input for data centers.

notes: Campaign site does not give his military branch or hometown.

name: Michael Thurow
bio: Mike Thurow is an independent candidate for Wisconsin's 6th Congressional District. He is a union fire captain from Mequon, Wisconsin. He has not previously held elected office.

platform.point: Would add federal oversight of utility and drug prices and break up food supply monopolies.
Would reinstate Glass-Steagall, strengthen the CFPB and keep private equity out of housing.
Wants Medicare to negotiate all drug prices and caps on drugs developed with taxpayer funds.
Backs a congressional stock trading ban, term limits, campaign finance reform and an end to gerrymandering.
Wants Congress to regulate AI and would back a law making data centers pay for their own energy use.
Would legalize marijuana to support farmers and cut incarceration costs.

economy.evidence: Supports Glass-Steagall, a stock buyback ban, antitrust action and federal utility price oversight.

welfare.evidence: Supports an expanded child tax credit, drug price caps and protecting Social Security from privatization.

security.evidence: Supports stronger consumer data protection and a ban on surveillance-based pricing.

foreign.evidence: Would shift defense spending from foreign interventions to veterans and domestic infrastructure.

tech.evidence: Calls for federal AI oversight and cost requirements for data centers.

notes: Campaigns as Mike Thurow; ballot name listed as Michael Thurow.

name: Michael Alfonso
bio: Michael Alfonso is the Republican nominee for Wisconsin's 7th Congressional District. Raised in Vilas County and Wausau, he earned a mathematics degree from UW-Madison and worked in construction and concrete. He later worked as a producer for The Dan Bongino Show and has not previously held elected office.

platform.point: Would cut federal spending and red tape so young families can afford homes.
Supports school choice and parental control over what children are taught.
Opposes abortion pills and supports state protections for the unborn from conception.
Would redirect money from foreign wars and aid to needs at home.
Would restrict large immigration programs to protect American workers' wages.
Supports banning stock trading by members of Congress.

economy.evidence: Calls for reining in federal spending, cutting red tape and returning power to the states.

liberty.evidence: Abortion: supports protections from conception and opposes abortion pills; guns: supports constitutional carry.

immigration.evidence: Would restrict mass immigration programs to protect American wages.

foreign.evidence: Would redirect spending from foreign wars and foreign aid to domestic needs.

education.evidence: Supports school choice and parental control over curriculum.

faith.evidence: Pledges to protect religious freedom and worship rights against government restrictions.

notes: The Commons photo is a candid event shot from December 2025 rather than a posed portrait.

name: Fred Clark
bio: Fred Clark is the Democratic nominee for Wisconsin's 7th Congressional District. He represented the Baraboo area in the Wisconsin State Assembly from 2009 to 2015 and was appointed to the state Natural Resources Board in 2019. A forester, he worked for the Wisconsin DNR and The Nature Conservancy, ran forestry and woodworking businesses, and is based in northern Wisconsin.

platform.point: Calls for federal action on housing, health care, child care and education costs.
Wants lower health costs and broader coverage.
Proposes building northern Wisconsin's economy on its natural assets and new income for farmers and forest owners.
Seeks border security combined with humane legal immigration that meets business needs.
Supports government guardrails on artificial intelligence and public oversight of data centers.

welfare.evidence: Calls for expanding health coverage and federal action on child care and health costs.

liberty.evidence: Abortion and contraception: supports reproductive freedom and full access to contraception.

immigration.evidence: Balances border security with humane legal immigration.

tech.evidence: Proposes government guardrails on AI and public oversight of data centers.

notes: The current issues page speaks of expanding coverage rather than universal coverage explicitly, so the welfare score may be high.

name: Tony Wied
bio: Tony Wied has represented Wisconsin's 8th Congressional District since November 2024, when he won a special election. Raised in Ashwaubenon and a graduate of St. Norbert College, he owned the Dino Stop chain of gas stations and convenience stores until 2022. He had not held elected office before Congress.

platform.point: Calls for immediate action to secure the southern border against drugs and trafficking.
Wants federal budgets balanced the way a small business manages its books.
Supports peace through strength and a strong military.
Would reduce regulations to expand domestic energy production.
Pledges to cut regulations on Wisconsin farmers.
Wants the U.S. to lead in cryptocurrency and blockchain development.

economy.evidence: Campaigns on cutting federal spending and reducing regulations.

immigration.evidence: Calls for immediate action to secure the southern border.

foreign.evidence: Supports peace through strength and maintaining military strength.

energy.evidence: Supports cutting regulations to expand American energy production.

tech.evidence: Wants the U.S. to lead in crypto and blockchain rather than cede ground to rivals.

notes: The border wall and Remain in Mexico details from earlier research were not visible on the current issues page.

name: Rick Crosson
bio: Rick Crosson is the Democratic nominee for Wisconsin's 8th Congressional District in northeast Wisconsin. He is a U.S. Army veteran who served in a combat unit, has held corporate board roles and has served on a school board.

platform.point: Would shift more of the tax burden onto the wealthiest individuals.
Would cap out-of-pocket costs and expand Medicare drug price negotiation.
Supports access to abortion decisions, IVF and contraception without political interference.
Opposes agricultural consolidation and supports right to repair and help for young farmers buying land.
Backs a well-resourced border, cleared visa backlogs and an earned path to legal status.
Pledges timely VA care, mental health services and recognition for Hmong veterans.

economy.evidence: Supports higher taxes on the wealthy and action against price-gouging and consolidation.

welfare.evidence: Would cap out-of-pocket health costs and protect Medicare and Social Security from cuts.

liberty.evidence: Abortion, IVF and contraception: supports access free of political restrictions.

immigration.evidence: Pairs border resources with visa modernization and an earned path to legal status.
